title: Object-oriented programming and data structures
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Design programs with classes and objects, use special methods, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism, work with two-dimensional lists, write recursive functions, implement merge sort and quicksort, and build stacks, queues and linked lists, at the level of AP Computer Science A and a first college course, taught in Python.
primary_reading: Problem Solving with Algorithms and Data Structures using Python (free, Runestone Academy)

blocks.deliverable: Write a bank-account class with tests.
Design a class from a written description.
Week 7 midterm; write a game-board class on a grid.
Implement merge sort and count its steps.
Implement a stack class and a queue class.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Object-oriented game or simulation: design (with a class diagram) and write a 200–300 line program, such as a card game, an ecosystem simulation or a library system, with at least four classes, inheritance, a grid or recursion, and tests.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
